newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: URC posts meagre growth in 1995/96 net.
newsitem.headline: URC posts meagre growth in 1995/96 net.

text.p: Universal Robina Corp (URC) said on Monday lower sale prices for its products and higher raw material costs limited its net income growth for the fiscal year 1995/96 (Oct-Sept).
URC, the food manufacturing subsidiary of conglomerate JG Summit Holdings Inc, said profits growth was meagre despite a double digit growth in turnover.
URC's net income totalled 1.29 billion pesos for the fiscal year 1995-1996, a 4.0 percent hike from 1.24 billion pesos posted in the previous year.
Net sales grew by 14 percent to 9.01 billion pesos from the year-ago 7.92 billion pesos, a consolidated financial statement submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission showed.

"URC's operating margins were reduced due primarily to lower selling prices for sugar and farm products and higher raw material costs, particularly wheat, corn and milk," the company said in its report.
Its consumer foods units registered a 23 percent revenue growth led by chocolate, snacks, candies and biscuits.
Its flour unit posted a 13 percent growth due to higher prices, while its corn products unit registered a 26 percent growth led by its duck and fish feed products.
The sugar milling unit saw a 29 percent decline in revenues due to reduction in selling prices.
The company said depreciation expenses rose by 26 percent due to the expansion of production capabilities, particularly for branded consumer foods.
However, URC expected a better year in 1996-1997 due to the opening of two new production facilities for its noodle products and a new sugar mill in central Negros island.

"URC management believes that prospects for 1996/97 look brighter, as operating margins are expected to improve due to the anticipated reduction in raw material costs, the continued strength of URC's higher margin branded consumer foods unit and increased refined sugar sales," the report added.
